diagnostic_evidence.quote: By Proposition~\ref{prop:convergence_iterative_surrogate}, the inequality~\eqref{eqn:proof_thm_2} achieves equality only when $\theta\left(\mathcal{F}\left(\bm{Q} \bm{z}_k^{(j+1)}\right)\\right) = \theta\left(\mathcal{F}\left(\bm{Q} \bm{z}_k^{(j)}\right)\right)$ except at the zero entries of $\bm{d}_k$ or at the zero entries of $\mathcal{F}\left(\bm{Q} \bm{z}_k^{(j+1)}\right)$ for all $k=1,2,\dots,N$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof establishes only the direction 'objective equality at the surrogate step implies stationarity of Phi at z^{(j+1)}'; the converse claimed by the iff is false. Counterexample: take a single scanning region with a probe Q having no zero entries and consistent noiseless data. The surrogate minimizer satisfies Q z^{(1)} = R(z^{(0)}, hence |F(Q z^{(1)})| = sqrt(d) and Phi(z^{(1)}) = 0 < Phi(z^{(0)}), while R(z^{(1)}) = R(z^{(0)}) gives nabla Phi(z^{(1)}) = conj(Q)(Q z^{(1)} - R(z^{(1)})) = 0. Thus nabla Phi(z^{(1)}) = 0 holds while Phi strictly decreased, falsifying 'nabla Phi(z^{(j+1)}) = 0 => Phi(z^{(j+1)}) = Phi(z^{(j)})'.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the 'iff' by the direction the proof actually establishes (Phi(z^{(j+1)}) = Phi(z^{(j)}) implies nabla Phi(z^{(j+1)}) = 0), or restate the optimality condition at the previous iterate (nabla Phi(z^{(j)}) = 0 implies Phi(z^{(j+1)}) = Phi(z^{(j)}), which follows from gradient agreement since z^{(j)} then minimizes the surrogate). No new argument is needed.
issues.overall_effect: The monotonic descent claim (the substantive part of the theorem) is unaffected, and the proved implication 'equality => stationarity' survives; only the optimality characterization is wrong. No labelled downstream result uses the converse: the rate theorem thm:convergence_rate relies solely on the monotone decrease and the descent inequality, so nothing formal is invalidated.
issues.title: Optimality 'iff' in the surrogate convergence theorem is false: stationarity at z^{(j+1)} does not imply objective equality
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local deletion/restatement of a false clause; every substantive guarantee (monotone descent, equality-implies-stationarity, the sublinear rate) is preserved and no dependent result is affected, so the loss of mathematical content is nil.

issues.failure_explanation: The expansion of Phi~(z; z^{(j)}) - Phi~(z^{(j)}; z^{(j)}) equals (1/2)(sum_k P_k^T |Q|^2) . |z - z^{(j)}|^2 + Re( (z - z^{(j)}) . nabla Phi(z^{(j)}) ). The proof's next line keeps the 1/2 in the quadratic term but drops it in the cross terms, writing them as conj(z - z^{(j)}) . nabla Phi + c.c. instead of (1/2)( conj(z-z^{(j)}) . nabla Phi + c.c. ) as the preceding line has. With the correct factor, the choice z = z^{(j)} - (1/L) nabla Phi with L = (1/2)||sum_k P_k^T |Q|^2||_inf gives Lt^2||nabla Phi||^2 - t||nabla Phi||^2 = 0 at t = 1/L: no descent at all. The stated bound min ||nabla Phi||^2 <= ||sum_k P_k^T |Q|^2||_inf Phi(z^{(0)}) / (2(n+1)) therefore does not follow; redoing the step with the correct factor and optimal stepsize t = 1/(2L) yields min ||nabla Phi||^2 <= 2 ||sum_k P_k^T |Q|^2||_inf Phi(z^{(0)}) / (n+1), i.e., a constant 4 times the one stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the descent lemma with the correct cross-term factor (1/2) and the optimized stepsize t = 1/||sum_k P_k^T |Q|^2||_inf, giving the bound min ||nabla Phi||^2 <= 2||sum_k P_k^T |Q|^2||_inf Phi(z^{(0)})/(n+1); this needs only a reoptimization of the stepsize, no new proof architecture.
issues.overall_effect: The sublinear O(1/n) guarantee for min_{0<=j<=n} ||nabla Phi(z^{(j)})||^2 survives only with a 4x larger constant; the advertised constant is unproven. The conclusion's claim of 'sub-linear convergence guarantees' is weakened in constant but not in rate type. No labelled formal result builds on this theorem.
issues.title: Convergence-rate proof drops a factor 1/2 in the cross terms, so the stated O(1/n) constant is unsupported; the honest constant is 4x larger
issues.why_classification: The dropped factor is load-bearing (with it the proof yields no descent), so the stated rate constant must be withdrawn and the argument redone with a different stepsize; however the guarantee type (sublinear O(1/n) in squared gradient norm) survives with a worse constant, which is a limited weakening leaving a recognizably comparable result.

issues.failure_explanation: Combining the two displayed identities reduces the proposition to I_h^H(1/(u+|Q|^2)) = 1/I_h^H(u+|Q|^2), i.e., that the reciprocal commutes with average pooling. This is false: for a bin with entries x_1,...,x_4 of u+|Q|^2, (1/4) sum_r 1/x_r differs from 1/((1/4) sum_r x_r) (e.g., x = (1,1,1,3) gives 5/6 vs 2/3; Jensen gives >= with strict inequality unless u+|Q|^2 is constant on the bin). The invoked lemmas (lem:unary, lem:binary) only justify commuting elementwise operations with the prolongation I_H^h (replication), not with the restriction I_h^H (averaging). The true relation is max|I_h^H e_k(g_2)|_r = (I_h^H 1/(u+|Q|^2))_r >= 1/(I_h^H(u+|Q|^2))_r = max|e_{H,k}(I_h^H g_1)|_r. Equality holds only when u+|Q|^2 is constant on every bin; for the rPIE choice u = alpha(|Q|_max^2 - |Q|^2) with the values alpha in {0.01, 0.02, 0.03, 0.06} actually used in the numerics, this fails on typical probes, so the equality is false in the advertised regime.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the claimed equality by the valid inequality max|e_{H,k}(I_h^H g_1)|_r <= max|I_h^H e_k(g_2)|_r (Jensen), with equality iff u+|Q|^2 is constant per bin; the weakened statement still certifies that coarse-level updates are controlled by fine-level ones without extra tuning.
issues.overall_effect: The proposition that formally justifies 'automatic hyperparameter selection' is false as stated; in reality the coarse-grid update magnitude is strictly smaller than the fine-grid one (so control is retained but exact matching is not). The abstract and introduction advertise automatic derivation of coarse-level hyperparameters, which is delivered only in the weakened one-sided sense. The stopping-criterion proposition prop:automatic_stopping_criterion_selection does not use this result and remains valid.
issues.title: Automatic regularization selection: claimed equality of coarse and fine update operator norms is false because restriction does not commute with the reciprocal
issues.why_classification: The proof's key identity is invalid and the exact-match claim fails in the parameter regime the paper uses; the supported repair is a one-sided weakening that retains a comparable control guarantee, so the advertised feature is materially but not fatally degraded.
